description:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates are compromised, Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirms on October 20.

An intermediate CA signs the certificates that websites present, so anyone holding one of these keys could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept.

title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software

title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA

description:
Cybersecurity researchers have released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for a recently patched critical security flaw impacting Fortinet FortiSIEM that could result in arbitrary code execution.

title: Critical FortiSIEM Flaw Gets Public Exploit PoC for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution

description:
A Chinese-speaking criminal pointed autonomous AI agents at company websites and let them break in with almost no help, and a security researcher watched it happen because the operators left their control panels open on the internet.

The agents tried more than 1,200 sites and reached websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm-equipment maker Deere, appliance company
title: Hackers Use Autonomous AI Agents to Breach Company Websites, Target Over 1,200 Sites

description:
The iPhone of Vladan Đokić, rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of Serbia's student protest movement, was infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware in 2026, the Citizen Lab said on October 19.

The finding came six days before Serbia's October 25 snap parliamentary election. The infection used a zero-click exploit, meaning Đokić did not have to tap a link or
title: Pegasus Spyware Infection Confirmed on Serbian University Rector's iPhone Days Before Election

ConnectWise on Monday said it has taken remediation measures, including strengthening administrative-access protections and resetting accounts and replacing application credentials, as it continues to respond to a security incident that led to unauthorized access to application identities associated with Cloud Backup.

title: ConnectWise Resets Credentials as Cloud Backup Remains Offline After Security Incident

description:
Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, released on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any certificate chain that passes through one of eight intermediate certificate authority keys.

Programs built on the new release will refuse connections to sites and services whose certificates were issued under those keys. The Go team says the keys belong to one certificate authority it has not
title: Go Issues Emergency Update Blocking Eight CA Keys Over Undisclosed Security Concerns

description: A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them
title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code

description:
WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's own privacy policy for Europe tells users they can complain to one.

The text sat in the pages' code, never shown on screen, until it was removed by October 18. Whether the
title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators

description:
An attacker used a contributor's GitHub account to replace the download archives on five existing releases of OVHcloud's command-line tool on Monday, October 19. The account had been hijacked, and the new files were a build designed to steal secrets stored on the disk of any machine that runs it, the cloud provider says.

They were live on GitHub for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC,
title: Hackers Hijack Five OVHcloud CLI Releases to Distribute Secret-Stealing Malware

description:

title: Ex-OpenAI Engineer Detained in Spy Device Case as Saudi Royal Contacts Emerge

description:
Siemens has addressed a DLL sideloading vulnerability impacting Siemens Software Center that it said has been exploited in ClickFix attacks.

description:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a ClickFix delivery platform called ROMULUS that's being used to distribute malware such as Legion Loader.

According to Forescout Research - Vedere Labs, ROMULUS is akin to a malware delivery service that employs ClickFix-style lures on bogus landing pages to trick unsuspecting users into running malicious commands and infecting their own
title: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware
